newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Syfrets launches fund after forex relaxation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Syfrets launches fund after forex relaxation.

text.p: Financial services group Syfrets said on Thursday it will launch a new offshore unit trust in the wake of changes to foreign exchange control regulations announced in Wednesday's 1997/1998 budget.
The Syfrets Universal Opportunities Fund, which will come to the market on March 17, will be wholly invested offshore, the group said in a statement.

"Now that institutions can invest 10 percent of their total assets under administration in international stock markets, we consider international funds a viable investment...hence, the timing of our launch," said Angela Delport, Syfrets' unit trusts product manager.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in his maiden budget that the 10-percent limit applicable to acquisitions of foreign portfolio assets will apply to all the assets under management of any specific unit trust scheme.
In addition, the definition of qualifying institutions for asset swaps will be widened to include regulated fund mangers.
The asset swap mechanism will also be widened and institutions will again be allowed to make foreign acquisitions during 1997 of up to three percent of the net inflows of funds last year, as in 1996.
Syfrets said the new fund's philosophy would be to aggressively maximise offshore exposure.
"The diversification of the fund's portfolio across countries, currencies and sectors is aimed at diversifying risk and reducing the volatility of the underlying investments," Syfrets said.
